description: A sixteen-step sequencer whose pattern is made by randomising and mutating rather than by setting steps one at a time, with sixteen memories to keep patterns in

params.text: The highest voltage a step's note can reach, a whole number of volts from 0 to 8
Copies the sequence into memory; pressing it writes the same pattern into all sixteen memories at once
Replaces the sequence with one from memory; pressing it brings back the sixteenth memory
Chooses what the sixteen lights show: at 0 the step now playing, at 1 which steps are switched on, at 2 the note voltage of each step as brightness
The chance that any one step is rerolled when MUTATE is pressed, none fully left and every step fully right
Rerolls the note voltage and the on-or-off state of each step separately, with the chance of any one step changing set by MUTATION RATE
How many steps the sequence runs before wrapping, 2 to 16
Draws a fresh random note voltage for all sixteen steps and switches each one on or off at the odds set by GATE/TRIG DENSITY
The chance that a step comes out switched on when the sequence is randomised, none fully left and all sixteen fully right
Sends the sequence back to its first step
Switches every step off and sets every note voltage to zero, leaving an empty sequence
Holds the NOTE output steady between steps, letting it change only when the sequence lands on a step that is switched on

inputs.text: A rising edge above 1V on a polyphonic channel copies the sequence into the memory of that number, so one cable can address all sixteen memories separately
A rising edge above 1V on a polyphonic channel replaces the sequence with the one in the memory of that number
A rising edge above 1V switches every step off and sets every note voltage to zero
A rising edge above 1V sends the sequence back to its first step
A rising edge above 1V draws a fresh random note for every step and rerolls which steps are switched on
A rising edge above 1V rerolls each step at the chance set by MUTATION RATE
A rising edge above 1V moves the sequence on by one step
A rising edge above 1V copies the current step's note to the NOTE output and holds it there

outputs.text: The position in the sequence as a voltage, 0V on the first step and 10V on the last
A 1ms pulse each time the sequence wraps from its last step back to its first
The note voltage of the step now playing, from 0V to the NOTE RANGE setting
10V while the step now playing is switched on, and 0V while it is off
A 1ms pulse each time the sequence lands on a step that is switched on

notes: the sixteen steps cannot be edited by hand: no knob or button exists for a step's note or its on-or-off state, and a pattern is built only with R'ND'M, MUTATE and ZERO.
a freshly added module has every step off and every note at zero, so it makes no sound at all until R'ND'M is pressed or a pattern is loaded from memory.
the SAVE and LOAD jacks are polyphonic and the channel number picks the memory; the panel buttons reach all sixteen at once, so they are worth one memory between them.
with AUTO S&H off and nothing patched to the S&H input, the NOTE output changes the instant the sequence steps, on steps that are switched off included.
